newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Huludao Zinc to launch 90 mln A share IPO.
newsitem.headline: China's Huludao Zinc to launch 90 mln A share IPO.

text.p: China's Huludao Zinc Industry Co Ltd, the world's largest zinc smelter, said on Friday it would launch an initial public offering (IPO) of 90 million domestic currency A shares for listing on the Shenzhen bourse.
The IPO, priced at 7.253 yuan per share, will kick off on June 11 and finish by June 18, Huludao said in a prospectus in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Shanghai-based China Guotai Securities was the lead underwriter for the offer, the prospectus said.

The net proceeds of nearly 653 million yuan ($80 million) expected to be raised would be used to boost production capacity of electrolytic zinc, one of the firm's main products, and to renovate smelting equipment, it said.
Huludao has an annual production capacity of 330,000 tonnes of various zinc products, including zinc ingots, the company said. The company also makes sulphuric acid.
The company, based in Huludao city in the northeastern province of Liaoning, currently holds 20 percent of China's zinc market and 2.5 percent of the world market, it said.
Huludao forecast a net profit of 189 million yuan for 1997 against 146.60 million yuan posted for 1996 and 147.98 million for the previous year based on Chinese accounting standards.
The company has said it was targeting sales of 2.66 billion yuan for this year, compared with 2.13 billion in 1996 and 2.26 billion a year earlier.

Huludao's performance was sensitive to foreign exchange rate fluctuations because about 50 percent of its zinc products were exported and about 20 percent of raw materials were imported from Canada, the United States and Australia.
After the A share offer, Huludao would have a total of 410 million shares, made up of 261.70 million institutional shares, 58.30 million employee-held shares and 90 million A shares.
